sentence1: More recently, IDH mutations and resultant 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG) production in leukemia cells were reported to induce global DNA hypermethylation through impaired TET2 catalytic function.

More importantly, Sentence 1 refers to 'global DNA hypermethylation' while Sentence 2 describes a 'hypermethylated promoter phenotype,' representing a meaningful difference in the scope and characterization of the epigenetic alteration. These distinctions prevent the meanings from being fully equivalent, but the sentences remain very highly aligned in semantic content.
